concept_gloss.applicability: Erkek ve kadın biçimlerinin çocuk ile köle yönlerini birlikte özetler; kadın kölede yaş sınırlaması bulunmadığını açıklama tamamlar.

error_profile.preserves: Yeni doğmuş çocuk ile erkek veya kadın köle arasındaki iki yönlü kapsamı korur.

concept_map.definition: Erkek biçimde yakın zamanda doğmuş çocuk veya ergenlik öncesi oğlan; kadın biçimde kız çocuk; ayrıca erkek ya da kadın köle. Kadın köle anlamı kişinin ileri yaşta olmasına karşın sürebilir.

facets.statement: Erkek biçimi yakın zamanda doğmuş çocuk veya ergenlik öncesi oğlan için kullanılır.
Erkek biçimi bir erkek köleyi de gösterebilir.
Kadın biçimi kız çocuğunu gösterebilir.
Kadın biçimi kadın köleyi gösterir ve bu kullanım ileri yaşta da geçerli olabilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Erkek biçimin yakın zamanda doğmuş çocuk anlamıyla kullanıldığı bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Erkek çocuk ve yakın zamanda doğmuşluk özelliklerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kadın biçimin köle anlamında, yaştan bağımsız kullanıldığı bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Kadın oluşu, kölelik konumunu ve yaş bağımsızlığını korur.

error_profile.loses: Erkek ve kadın köle anlamlarını, ayrıca yaştan bağımsız kadın köle kullanımını kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Yakın zamanda doğmuş küçük çocuk yönünü korur.

error_profile.adds: Özgür ve ücretli çalışanları da kapsama sokabilir.
error_profile.collision: Hizmet görevi ile kişinin kölelik konumunu birbirine karıştırır.
error_profile.loses: Yeni doğmuş çocuk anlamını ve kölelik konumunun açık sınırını kaybeder.
error_profile.preserves: Bir başkasına hizmet eden kişi çağrışımını kısmen korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Erkek biçimin çocuk yönü yeni doğmuş çocuk yanında ergenlik öncesi oğlanı da kapsar; kadın biçimi kız çocuğu ve kadın köle için kullanılır, köle anlamı özellikle kadın biçiminde yaş şartına bağlı değildir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi erkek biçimi için yeni doğmuş çocuk, ergenlik öncesi oğlan ve erkek köleyi; kadın biçimi için kız çocuk ile kadın köleyi birlikte verir. Dal çerçevesindeki çocuk ve köle yönleri uygundur, ancak çocuk yönü yalnız yeni doğmuşlukla sınırlandırılamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: yeni doğmuş erkek çocuk; erkek köle

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimlerin çocuk ve köle yönlerini birlikte korur; genel çocuk anlamı veya herhangi bir hizmetçilik ilişkisi içeri alınmaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilenler kadın köle, küçük yavru, gençlik adıyla köle ve genel çocuk sınırlarını açıkça karşılaştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal çocuk ve köle yönlerini cinsiyet biçimleriyle birlikte taşır; komşu dal bu çoklu yapıdan yalnız kadın köle anlamını ayırır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal erkek çocuk, özellikle yeni doğmuş çocuk veya ergenlik öncesi oğlan, kız çocuk ve erkek köleyi de kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yalnız kadın köle anlamına odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Kadın köle anlamı iki dalın doğrudan kesişimidir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal köle anlamına uzanır ve insan kullanımlarında kalır; komşu dal köleliği içermez, küçük olmayı hayvan yavrularına kadar genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal insan çocuğunun yanında erkek veya kadın köle anlamını da taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal küçük insan çocuğuyla birlikte evcil ve yabani hayvan yavrularını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Küçük insan çocuğu iki dalın kesiştiği alandır; bu dal erkek biçimde yeni doğmuş veya ergenlik öncesi oğlanı, kadın biçimde kız çocuğunu kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın çocuk yönü erkek biçimde yeni doğmuş veya ergenlik öncesi oğlanı, kadın biçimde kız çocuğunu kapsar; komşu dal genç kişi adlarını köle ve hizmetçi için örtülü bir söyleyiş olarak kullanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal erkek çocuk, özellikle yeni doğmuş veya ergenlik öncesi oğlan, ve kız çocuk anlamını taşır; köle kullanımını da bu adlandırma alanıyla birlikte verir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: çocuk veya köle / genç diye anılan köle
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal genç erkek ve kız adlarını köle veya hizmetçi için örtülü biçimde kullanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Erkek ve kadın kölenin yaş bildiren bir adla gösterilmesi iki dalı yaklaştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal biçime bağlı çocuk kapsamıyla köle anlamını birleştirir; komşu dal köleliği dışarıda bırakıp çocukluk bağını yaş ve sayı bakımından geniş tutar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal erkek biçimde yeni doğmuş veya ergenlik öncesi oğlanı, kadın biçimde kız çocuğunu kapsar ve ayrıca köle anlamı taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal çocuğu her yaşta, her cinsiyette ve tek ya da çok kişi olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İnsan çocuğu iki dalda da yer alır; bu dal erkek biçimde yeni doğmuş veya ergenlik öncesi oğlanı, kadın biçimde kız çocuğunu gösterir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: الوليدة الأنثى والجمع ولائد (maqayis)؛ الوليد الصبي والعبد والجمع ولدان وولدة؛ الوليد الصبية والأمة والجمع الولائد (sihah)؛ الوليد الصبي حين يولد؛ يقال للأمة وليدة وإن كانت مسنة (tahdhib)؛ الوليد يقال لمن قرب عهده بالولادة؛ الوليدة مختصة بالإماء في عامة كلامهم (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kanıt erkek biçimi yeni doğmuş çocuk, ergenlik öncesi oğlan ve erkek köleye; kadın biçimi kız çocuk ile kadın köleye dağıtır. Kadın köle adlandırmasının ileri yaşta da kullanılabildiği ayrıca belirtilir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الوليد للصبي أو الغلام القريب العهد بالولادة، والوليدة للصبية أو الأمة، وما جمعه ولدان أو ولائد بحسب النص.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل هنا الولد العام للصغير والكبير، ولا التليدة أو المولدة إلا إذا دل السياق على الجارية أو العبد المولود في الملك.

concept_gloss.applicability: Nedene bağlı ortaya çıkma çekirdeğiyle sonradan oluşturulmuş, uydurulmuş ve katışıksız olmayan uzantıları birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: Kaynak ile sonuç arasındaki neden bağını ve sonradan üretilmiş olma yönünü korur.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyden nedenle türeme veya sonradan oluşturulma

concept_map.definition: Belirli söz biriminde bir şeyin başka bir şeyden bir neden aracılığıyla ortaya çıkması. Buna bağlı olarak sonradan oluşturulan söz, uydurulan kitap veya kanıt ve katışıksız sayılmayan dil ya da kişi de kendi biçim ve kalıplarında nitelenir.

facets.statement: Belirli söz biriminde bir şey, başka bir şeyden bir neden aracılığıyla ortaya çıkar.
Sonradan oluşturulan söz bu ortaya çıkma düşüncesinin bir uzantısıdır.
Uydurulmuş kitap ve doğrulanmamış, üretilmiş kanıt aynı niteleme alanındadır.
Katışıksız sayılmayan dil veya kişi için de bu niteleme kullanılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sonucun başka bir şeyden belirli bir nedenle çıktığı süreçlerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kaynak, neden ve ortaya çıkan sonuç arasındaki bağı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Daha önce bulunmayıp sonradan üretilen bir söz veya benzeri oluşum için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Sonradan ortaya çıkarılmış olma özelliğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gerçekliği bulunmayan veya doğrulanmamış kitap ve kanıt gibi örneklerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gerçek olmayıp sonradan üretilmiş olma yönünü korur.

error_profile.loses: Ortaya çıkışın neden bağını, sürecini ve sonradan oluşturulmuş ya da uydurulmuş nitelemelerini kaybeder.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Yaş bakımından denk kişi iki dalın kesiştiği alandır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği aynı yaşta olan denk kişidir; tekil, ikili ve çoğul biçim bilgileri bu yaştaşlık ilişkisini sayı bakımından çeşitlendirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız kanıtta verilen sabit söyleyişin anlamını karşılar; yalın bir sözcük anlamı olarak kullanılamaz.

concept_gloss.text: çok büyük bir durum ya da pek bol bir şey

concept_map.definition: Yalnız belirli bir kalıp söz içinde, çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ya da çok bol bir şeyi anlatır. Söyleyişin kökeni baskına bağlanır; çok yiyecek ve çok otlak bolluk örnekleridir.

facets.statement: Kalıp söz çok büyük, önemli veya ağır bir durumu anlatır.
Aynı kalıp söz çok bol bir şeyi anlatmak için de kullanılır.
Söyleyişin çıkışı, baskın sırasında yaşanan ağır duruma bağlanır.
Çok yiyecek ve çok otlak, bolluk yönünün açık örnekleridir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz büyük, önemli ve ağır bir olay veya durum için söylendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Durumun olağanüstü büyüklük ve ağırlık derecesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıp söz yiyecek veya otlak gibi bir şeyin çokluğunu anlatırken kullanılır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız verilen kalıp sözde geçerlidir; tek başına çocuk adını veya bu kalıp dışında kalan her büyüklük ve bolluk durumunu kapsamaz.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yalnız sabit bir söyleyiş içinde çok büyük veya ağır bir durumu ve çok bol bir şeyi anlatır; kökeni baskına bağlar, yiyecek ve otlağı bolluk örnekleri olarak verir. Ön çerçevedeki süt örneği yetkili kaynak ifadesinde bulunmadığından tanım bu örneği dışarıda bırakacak biçimde yeniden kurulmalıdır.

text.arabic_uthmani: وَقُلِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًۭا وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ شَرِيكٌۭ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلِىٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّ ۖ وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًۢا

baseline.text: De ki: Çocuk edinmeyen, hükümranlığında ortağı olmayan ve acizlikten ötürü bir koruyucusu bulunmayan Allah'a hamdolsun. O'nu gereğince büyük bil.

findings.text: Çocuk, ortak ve acizlikten doğan yardımcı ihtiyacının art arda kaldırılması, Allah'ın büyüklüğünü soy, koalisyon veya kurtarıcı desteğine dayanmayan yapısal bağımsızlık olarak belirler; büyütmek yalnız sesi artırmak değildir.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech makes the verse a performed proclamation rather than a silent inventory.
Praise opposed to blame gives the proclamation its evaluative center.
Rightful greatness and majesty make the verb-masdar close an emphatic act of exaltation.

changed_reading.after: The ayah commands a voiced verdict: convert the three negated dependencies into praise and emphatic magnification.
changed_reading.before: The ayah lists divine attributes and appends praise.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative sequence قُلِ ... ٱلْحَمْدُ ... وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا frames the ayah as an enacted utterance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Speech externalizes praise, the three negations supply its grounds, and the doubled closing root turns recognition of greatness into the commanded culmination.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition for oneself casts taking a child as adding a support or possession.
Born offspring supplies the lineage relation explicitly excluded from divine identity.
Participation between multiple parties supplies the divided claim denied within dominion.
Sovereignty and rule define the field in which participation is excluded.
Taking charge of another's affair supplies the external support that God does not require.
Abasement under coercion states the deficit from which such protective support would arise.

changed_reading.after: The coordinated denials map one mechanism: sovereignty needing neither dynastic continuation, shared administration, nor rescue from weakness.
changed_reading.before: The verse separately denies three associates of God.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three coordinated لَمْ clauses deny a child, a partner in the dominion, and an ally arising from humiliation.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence closes three routes by which human rule is stabilized: acquired lineage, divided title, and protective patronage. Divine dominion is therefore not merely singular but structurally nondependent.

activation_trace.role: Gentle direction to the right way supplies the guidance on which the creature depends.
Supportive alliance names the rescuing relation creatures cannot secure elsewhere.
Otherness marks the failed search for a protector apart from God.
The same supportive alliance is denied as a relation God would need for Himself.
Coerced abasement identifies the deficiency that could necessitate a protector, then excludes it from God.

changed_reading.after: God is the sought source of protection, not a vulnerable being whose sovereignty must be repaired by a protector.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening context makes creatures dependent on divine guidance and unable to find protective allies apart from Him; the focus reverses the relation by denying that God Himself needs an ally because of abasement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored ally language and opposite dependency positions; I infer a protector/protected reversal, while a live alternative is that each clause only rejects false patrons locally.
structural_cues: 17:97 denies finding allies apart from Him, while 17:111 denies an ally for Him arising from humiliation.

activation_trace.role: Something arising from another supplies the derivative-production possibility that the child clause excludes.
Innovative bringing-into-being supplies the challenged act of renewed creation.
New occurrence after rupture makes recreation follow bodily disintegration without lineage.
Repeated origination joins cosmic creation to the creation of beings like the challengers.
Effective capacity supplies the power by which origination reaches action.
Likeness supplies reproducible creatures without making them divine offspring.

changed_reading.after: The clause separates God's abundant power to originate and re-originate from the creaturely mechanism of deriving continuity through offspring.
changed_reading.before: The child clause is a bare denial of offspring.

context_deltas.mechanism: The resurrection challenge moves from disintegrated remains to new creation and then to cosmic creation and capacity. Against that display of origination, denying a child distinguishes sovereign creation from genealogical self-extension rather than suggesting an absence of generative power.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies derivative offspring, newness after rupture, origination, likeness, and effective capacity; I infer a contrast between genealogy and creation, while the narrower alternative is a denial of offspring with no theory of production implied.
structural_cues: 17:98 asks whether bones and fragments can become a new creation; 17:99 answers through creation of the heavens, earth, and beings like them.

activation_trace.role: Sovereignty supplies the divine dominion whose mode is clarified by the human counterexample.
Possession and disposal place the imagined treasuries under human control.
Secured storage supplies the bounded-resource image that invites hoarding.
Merciful tenderness identifies what human ownership would constrict.
Miserly retention supplies the failed human administration of mercy.
Expenditure of wealth supplies the imagined loss that produces withholding.
Constriction and reduction diagnose the scarcity logic of human control.

changed_reading.after: Unshared dominion also means mercy cannot be rationed by a scarcity-bound co-owner who fears that giving will exhaust the store.

context_deltas.mechanism: The hypothetical in 17:100 puts mercy's treasuries under human ownership and immediately yields hoarding from fear of depletion. The focus's unshared dominion then reads as freedom from scarcity-conditioned co-management: mercy is not exposed to a parsimonious partner's veto.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a conditional chain from human ownership through fear of spending to constriction; I carry that chain into the focus's unshared dominion, while the alternative is that 17:100 criticizes humans without explaining why dominion has no partner.
structural_cues: 17:100 and 17:111 are both قُلْ declarations linking م ل ك to sharply different human and divine modes of rule.

activation_trace.role: Sovereignty supplies the focus anchor against which the preceding contest of rule is read.
Destabilizing lightness supplies the attempted removal of a people from their ground.
Caused drowning supplies the reversal that terminates the coercer's project.
Undivided completeness makes the reversal encompass the ruler and all with him.
Settled habitation reverses the attempted displacement.
A mixed collectivity gathered as one supplies the later reorganization of dispersed people.

changed_reading.after: It also closes the Pharaoh sequence as a judgment that coercive possession of land is not a durable share in ultimate rule.
changed_reading.before: The denial of a partner in dominion is an abstract exclusivity claim.

context_deltas.mechanism: The confrontation with Pharaoh culminates in an attempt to shake a people from the land, followed by the coercer's drowning, the people's settlement, and their later gathering as a mixed whole. The focus's unpartnered dominion becomes a verdict on coercive rule that cannot secure its own project.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies displacement, drowning, settlement, and gathering; I assign their reversal as evidence about sovereignty in 17:111, while they may instead remain historical acts without an institutional gloss.
structural_cues: 17:101-102 stage the confrontation with Pharaoh; 17:103-104 reverse attempted expulsion into drowning, settlement, and eventual gathering.

activation_trace.role: Rightful greatness supplies the upward pole recognized by the final imperative.
Abasement under coercion marks the lowering explicitly excluded from God.
Audible, unsteady falling gives recognition of revelation a downward bodily vector.
Prostrating lowliness turns the fall into willing worship rather than defeat.
Increase and growth create the paradoxical upward measure of a deepening low posture.
Humble lowering names what grows as divine greatness is recognized.

changed_reading.after: Magnification is tested by a reversal in the worshipper: recognition rises as the knowledgeable body and self voluntarily lower.
changed_reading.before: Magnifying God is chiefly an upward verbal assertion.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those given knowledge repeatedly fall, prostrate, and increase in humility. The upward semantic force of magnifying God is therefore paired with the knower's voluntary bodily lowering, sharply unlike the coerced humiliation denied of God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated falling, prostration, increasing humility, and emphatic magnification; I infer a reciprocal vertical axis, while the alternative treats these as adjacent but independent devotional acts.
structural_cues: يَخِرُّونَ is repeated in 17:107 and 17:109, and the upward verb يَزِيدُ takes خُشُوعًا as its result immediately before the repeated ك ب ر close.

activation_trace.role: Deeming something great in the breast supplies semantic magnification without prescribing maximal loudness.
Public declaration and raised sound supply the upper vocal extreme explicitly barred.
Secret, lowered utterance supplies the opposite vocal extreme explicitly barred.
A state intermediate between two ends supplies the calibration principle.
A traversable extended path turns calibration into a sustained practice rather than a midpoint abstraction.

changed_reading.after: Magnify Him without mistaking decibels for greatness: emphatic recognition remains compatible with the measured vocal path just prescribed.
changed_reading.before: كَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا may suggest making praise as loud or externally large as possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding instruction rejects both raised proclamation and inaudibility in prayer and commands a traversable middle way. Emphatic magnification in 17:111 therefore cannot be equated with maximizing acoustic force; it names the magnitude of recognition within a calibrated voice.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit vocal bounds followed by emphatic takbir; I infer that adjacency blocks a loudness reading, while the live alternative confines the bounds to prayer and leaves the next imperative acoustically unspecified.
structural_cues: The two vocal prohibitions in 17:110 immediately precede 17:111's قُلِ and emphatic verb-masdar magnification.

remaining_uncertainties: The creation context strongly supports a creation-versus-genealogy contrast, but the derivative-production branch of و ل د remains broader than the ordinary offspring sense.
The political reading is structurally visible through explicit dominion and the Pharaoh reversal, but its institutional detail is analogical.
The prayer-volume rule may govern only 17:110 locally even though its adjacency sharply constrains a loudness reading of 17:111.
strongest_changes: The 17:100 ownership counterfactual turns unshared dominion into freedom from scarcity-driven withholding of mercy.
The ally language in 17:97 reverses the dependency relation: creatures seek protection from God, whereas God needs no protector from abasement.
The 17:107-110 sequence calibrates takbir through voluntary lowering and a voice between loudness and inaudibility.
summary.what_was_special: Repeated focus roots and mirrored constructions made the context unusually diagnostic: م ل ك contrasts human and divine control, و ل ي reverses protector and protected, and the final ك ب ر imperative arrives after both bodily descent and vocal calibration.

activation_trace.role: Offspring supplies the dynastic-continuity slot in the analogy.
Multi-party participation supplies the co-regency slot in the analogy.
Sovereignty makes institutional rule an explicit rather than free-floating comparison.
Administrative guardianship supplies the patron or regent slot in the analogy.
Destabilization supplies the coercive sovereign practice whose durability is tested.
Settlement supplies the divine reversal of attempted territorial removal.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they also dismantle the familiar architecture of fragile regimes: dynasty, co-rule, and emergency patronage are all unnecessary to divine dominion.
changed_reading.before: The three negations are only a list of metaphysical exclusions.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads metaphysical relation nouns through institutional supports of rule. It remains anchored in child, partner, dominion, ally, and the displacement-settlement reversal; downstream prose should present it as a political analogy, not the verse's exclusive referent or a historical identification.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: وَلَدًا, شَرِيكٌ فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ, and وَلِىٌّ form three relation slots around explicit dominion.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Praise removes every dependency-model before affirming greatness.** `ح م د:B001/B003` praise and praiseworthy fullness, `ء خ ذ:B010` taking for oneself, `و ل د:B005` generated derivative, `ش ر ك:B001` partnership, `م ل ك:B002/B003` ownership/dominion, `و ل ي:B004` support, `ذ ل ل:B001` abasement, and `ك ب ر:B001/B003` greatness and regarding as great. Three negations remove offspring, shared rule, and rescuing ally. I infer true magnification requires subtracting inherited models of succession, coalition, and weakness. The ending reads *takbīr* as disciplined conceptual purification, not sheer intensification.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: No later ayah follows in the packet, so no later retrospective activation emerged. The ayah closes the walk by converting prior contrasts between creaturely dependence and divine sufficiency into purified praise.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Greatness as structural independence rather than vocal magnitude.** Lexical evidence: `ح م د B001` (praise opposite blame) in `ٱلْحَمْدُ`, `ش ر ك B001` (sharing and partnership) in `شَرِيكٌ`, `م ل ك B003` (kingship and dominion) in `ٱلْمُلْكِ`, `و ل ي B004` (loyal alliance and support) in `وَلِىٌّ`, `ذ ل ل B001` (abasement under overpowering) in `ٱلذُّلِّ`, and `ك ب ر B001` (greatness opposite smallness) in `كَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا`. Structural cue: 17:110 first calibrates prayer away from loudness and gathers many names under one possessor; this ayah then negates lineage, shared dominion, and compensatory alliance before commanding magnification. Assigned role: the three negations remove genealogical continuation, divided rule, and support required by weakness; praise affirms the resulting independence. Abductive move: the packet places conceptual negations after acoustic calibration; I infer that true magnification concerns dependency-structure rather than volume. Reading change: `تَكْبِيرًا` culminates the surah by enlarging the understanding of divine independence, not by merely intensifying sound.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: No later ayah exists within the clipped focus window; the retrospective pass found no later surprise beyond 17:111's own closing independence structure.

words.gloss_range: resumptive and connective opening particle launching the final commanded doxology
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the closing verse as more than a spare connector. It resumes after the prayer-volume instruction of 17:110 and fuses immediately into the command to say, so the surah lands in performed praise rather than in detached summary.

topics.headline: resumptive opening into praise command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final ayah opens as a fresh commanded praise declaration while still carrying forward the boundary from 17:110.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows converge on resumptive opening, command framing, and the 17:110 boundary; QAC and attachment evidence allow either istiʾnāf or coordination, with the local clause introducing commanded speech.

words.gloss_range: direct Form I command to speak the following praise formula
words.prose: {{ar:قُلِ}} ({{tr:quli}}) makes the closing theology vocal. The 2ms imperative carries the addressee from 17:110 into a second commanded utterance, while the liaison into {{ar:ٱلْحَمْدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamdu}}) makes command and content touch in recitation. The surah closes by telling the hearer what to say.
words.root_gloss_range: saying and commanded utterance; local imperative selects direct vocal declaration

topics.headline: commanded speech as worship act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the theology is assigned to the addressee as speech to perform, not merely doctrine to observe.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I 2ms imperative governing the quoted praise content, and the CRITICAL rows preserve the boundary echo with 17:110 plus the performative force of saying.

words.gloss_range: definite nominative praise as a comprehensive standing category assigned to God
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَمْدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamdu}}) names praise as a definite, nominative category, then lets {{ar:لِلَّهِ}} ({{tr:li-llāhi}}) assign it. The root can sit near thanks and commendation, but here the following denials narrow the force toward praise for what God is: untouched by offspring, co-rule, or need. The formula also returns to the Quranic praise opening (1:2) while framing the surah-final magnification.
words.root_gloss_range: praise, commendation, recognition of excellence; local form selects inherent praise rather than mere thanks for a benefit

topics.headline: all praise as stable divine due
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening gives the whole category of praise to God before the negations explain why.
topics.reason: The word is a definite gerund functioning as subject; semantic rows distinguish ḥamd from shukr, while formula and closure rows support the praise-frame without replacing the local syntax.

words.gloss_range: attribution and possession preposition completing the praise predicate
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) turns the praise noun into an assignment: praise belongs to God and is due to God. Because it functions in the predicate of the nominal clause, the particle lets the category appear first and then resolves its rightful owner.

topics.headline: praise assigned as belonging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that praise is not merely aimed toward God but grammatically belongs to Him.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the preposition as governing the divine name and completing the nominal predication; the CRITICAL rows preserve possession, due attribution, fusion, and word order.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as possessor and endpoint of the praise formula
words.prose: {{ar:لَّهِ}} ({{tr:li-llāhi}}) compresses the attribution lām and the divine name into the predicate of praise. The root-dispute background may keep worship and seeking near the name, but the local grammar is firmer: the named God from the 17:110 invocation boundary is now the one to whom all praise belongs.
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship and seeking associations in the disputed root background; local function remains the named divine referent

topics.headline: divine name as praise possessor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the invoked name from 17:110 becomes the possessor of all praise in 17:111.
topics.reason: The proper-name function and genitive governance constrain the broader root discussion; CRITICAL boundary rows and formula rows remain useful because they show the name changing from invocation target to praise possessor.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular relative pronoun binding the three denials to the divine name
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) fastens the whole sequence of denials to the divine name. Its masculine singular agreement routes the clauses to God rather than to the praise noun, and the order moves from child to partner to patron as a structured inventory of denied dependency.

topics.headline: relative clause as denial block
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the three negations are one identifying description of God, not loose afterthoughts after praise.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the relative clause modify the divine name, and the CRITICAL rows coherently treat the following no-child, no-partner, no-patron sequence as one descriptive block.

words.gloss_range: first past-negating jussive particle initiating the triadic denial cadence
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) starts the middle cadence. It governs the following jussive and gives the denial continuing force: no taking of offspring has occurred or stands valid. Because the particle will recur twice, this first beat also opens the triad of denied relations.

topics.headline: first enduring negation beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the no-child claim begins a repeated, enduring negation pattern rather than a one-off past report.
topics.reason: QAC marks jussive governance and past negation; CRITICAL rows add the repeated lam pattern and cumulative exclusion across child, partner, and patron.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII jussive taking-for-oneself, locally denying offspring adoption or claiming
words.prose: {{ar:يَتَّخِذْ}} ({{tr:yattakhidh}}) is not a bare birth verb. Under {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}), the Form VIII verb denies taking-for-oneself: adoption, appropriation, or claimed offspring. The hand-grasp root image survives as possessive pressure, but the local collocation with {{ar:وَلَدًا}} ({{tr:waladan}}) keeps the point on claimed child-relation. It also places the first denial inside a recurring no-offspring formula field (19:35, 25:2, 39:4).
words.root_gloss_range: taking, grasping, seizing, adopting, claiming; local collocation selects self-directed taking of a child, not ordinary grasping alone

topics.headline: self-directed offspring claiming denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial reaches adoptive or possessive claiming of offspring and belongs to a recurring no-offspring formula, not only biological begetting.
topics.reason: QAC identifies Form VIII jussive and an explicit object; V4 and CRITICAL semantic rows support taking-for-oneself while the local object narrows the broad root to offspring-claim denial.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative offspring object under negation, covering any child category
words.prose: {{ar:وَلَدًۭا}} ({{tr:waladan}}) is the accusative object of the denied taking verb. Its singular indefiniteness under negation does not make the denial small; it excludes the offspring category at its minimal instance. The root image of produced progeny remains visible, while the local grammar blocks a narrow male-child-only reading. In the surah-local frame, that broad offspring denial also separates God from earlier human children language and the satanic sharing-in-offspring scene (17:64).
words.root_gloss_range: birth, begetting, offspring, produced progeny; local singular indefinite under negation universalizes the category

topics.headline: any offspring category denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object is any offspring whatsoever, broader than a specific son, while also closing off the surah’s earlier human and satanic offspring fields.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence makes the noun the direct object of {{ar:يَتَّخِذْ}} ({{tr:yattakhidh}}); CRITICAL rows and lexical evidence support broad offspring coverage, indefiniteness, and surah-local child language.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle opening the second full negation clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the sequence additive. By joining a new {{ar:لَمْ يَكُن}} ({{tr:lam yakun}}) clause, it makes the partner denial coequal with the child denial and preserves the enumerated architecture of dependencies being removed one by one.

topics.headline: second denial added as coequal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that partnerlessness is a separate axis of denial, not merely an explanation of childlessness.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark coordination; the CRITICAL rows focus on the particle preserving a second full negation unit.

words.gloss_range: second jussive negator transferring the enduring denial into an existential clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) repeats the negative force but changes the verb type that follows. The ayah moves from denied action to denied being, so the middle clause is not just another event report; it denies a state of partnership.

topics.headline: from denied action to denied state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from no act of taking to no state of having a partner, while the negation force stays parallel.
topics.reason: The second lam governs {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}) in QAC and maintains the same repeated negation pattern identified by the CRITICAL rows.

words.gloss_range: apocopated existential verb under negation, denying the existence of a partner-state
words.prose: {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}) is the shortened jussive being-verb under {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}). Its frame, {{ar:لَهُۥ شَرِيكٌ}} ({{tr:lahu sharīkun}}), first sets the relation to God and then denies any partner as existent. The following dominion phrase locates that nonexistence inside sovereign rule, preparing the repeated template that will return with the patron noun.
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, occurring; local negated copular frame selects nonexistence of the relational subject

topics.headline: existence of co-rule denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the partner is denied at the level of existence within God’s dominion, not merely as an unchosen assistant.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form I imperfect jussive with a following subject and possessive PP; CRITICAL rows support existential denial, apocopation, and the repeated {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) template.

words.gloss_range: fronted possessive dative pronoun framing the denied partner as relation to God
words.prose: {{ar:لَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) puts the relation to God in front of the partner noun. The phrase can carry possession, belonging, and existential availability together, so the clause denies any partner as something that could be for Him or within His sphere.

topics.headline: God’s sphere framed before the partner noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause places God’s possessive frame before naming the denied partner.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the PP as the fronted predicate/complement of the negated copular clause; CRITICAL rows preserve its information-structure pressure and repetition with word20.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative co-sharer noun denied as subject of the existential clause
words.prose: {{ar:شَرِيكٌۭ}} ({{tr:sharīkun}}) is the delayed nominative subject whose existence is denied. Its indefinite form under negation opens the category only to close it completely: no partner of any kind. The root’s sharing and snare imagery can color co-rule as entanglement, while {{ar:فِى ٱلْمُلْكِ}} ({{tr:fī al-mulki}}) narrows the local target to shared dominion.
words.root_gloss_range: sharing, partnership, association, entanglement; local phrase selects a co-holder in dominion, not merely the human act of associating

topics.headline: any co-holder in dominion excluded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah denies any co-holder inside sovereignty, not just a vague associate.
topics.reason: The noun is syntactically the subject of {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}); V4 and CRITICAL rows support co-sharer semantics, indefiniteness, formula field, and the local dominion scope.

words.gloss_range: domain-marking preposition locating the partner denial within dominion
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) gives the second denial its domain. Whether the phrase attaches to the partner noun or to the whole copular clause, it makes dominion the conceptual interior in which no co-holder exists.

topics.headline: dominion as the denial’s domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the partner denial is scoped to the inside of sovereign rule.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence allows local attachment to {{ar:شَرِيكٌ}} ({{tr:sharīkun}}) or the clause while preserving the same domain function; CRITICAL rows are coherent with that ambiguity.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive dominion as comprehensive sphere of sovereign possession
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُلْكِ}} ({{tr:al-mulki}}) is genitive after {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) and names the domain in which no partner is allowed. The root can range across ownership and kingship, but the local abstract noun points to sovereign rule itself, with the grip image making the domain feel held rather than merely titled.
words.root_gloss_range: owning, possessing, gripping, ruling, kingship; local abstract noun selects the domain of rule rather than a ruler title

topics.headline: unshared sovereign grip
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied partnership is inside total sovereign dominion, pictured as God’s unshared grip.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a definite abstract noun governed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}); CRITICAL rows support comprehensiveness, grip imagery, and distinction from a ruler-title.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle opening the third full negation clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds a third full clause. It prevents the patron denial from collapsing into the partner denial and keeps the chain ordered: offspring, co-rule, then protective dependency before the final command.

topics.headline: third denial kept separate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that vulnerability-based patronage is a third separate dependency, not a modifier of co-rule.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the third negation with the second; CRITICAL rows agree that the particle preserves a separate, cumulative denial.

words.gloss_range: third jussive negator completing the repeated dependency-denial frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) completes the threefold negation architecture. The repeated particle keeps the patron denial under the same temporal and grammatical force as the first two denials, so the ayah’s center reads as a systematic inventory.

topics.headline: third negation completes the triad
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the no-patron clause receives the same enduring negation as the no-child and no-partner clauses.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle governing the second {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}); the CRITICAL rows preserve repeated cadence and exhaustive dependency denial.

words.gloss_range: second apocopated existential verb, paralleling the partner clause for the patron denial
words.prose: {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}) repeats the compact existential denial from word12. The verb is the same, but the denied subject changes from {{ar:شَرِيكٌ}} ({{tr:sharīkun}}) to {{ar:وَلِيٌّ}} ({{tr:waliyyun}}), making the two copular clauses twins with different dependency targets.
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, occurring; local negated copular frame denies the existence of the patron relation

topics.headline: existence of patron-state denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the patron relation never has being for God, in the same structure that denied a partner.
topics.reason: The repeated jussive form and fronted {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) frame are supported by QAC and attachment evidence; CRITICAL rows focus on structural parity and changed denied noun.

words.gloss_range: second possessive dative pronoun repeating the frame for the patron denial
words.prose: {{ar:لَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) repeats the possessive frame exactly. The same pronoun holds the divine referent steady while the noun slot changes, turning the two clauses into a visible template: no partner for Him, no patron for Him.

topics.headline: same frame, new denied noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated no-X-for-Him template that makes partner and patron comparable while keeping them distinct.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the phrase as the possessive predicate/complement in the second copular clause; CRITICAL rows stress repetition, fusion, and the swapped noun slot.

words.gloss_range: indefinite patron/protector noun, locally selected as compensatory support from lowliness
words.prose: {{ar:وَلِىٌّۭ}} ({{tr:waliyyun}}) names a close-standing patron as the subject denied by the second {{ar:يَكُن}} ({{tr:yakun}}). The root’s nearness field is real, but {{ar:مِّنَ ٱلذُّلِّ}} ({{tr:min al-dhulli}}) narrows the local sense toward compensatory protection: no guardian or patron arises for God from weakness or lowliness.
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, adjacency, guardianship, patronage, alliance, protection; local phrase selects vulnerability-based protective patronage

topics.headline: no close protector born of need
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied relation is not ordinary companionship but a protector needed because of vulnerability.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as nominative subject under negation; CRITICAL and V4 rows support the range from ally to guardian while the following PP selects the vulnerability-protection sense.

words.gloss_range: source, cause, or explicative preposition routing lowliness into the no-patron clause
words.prose: {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) is the hinge of the third denial. It can attach to the patron noun, the being verb, or the whole clause, so the phrase can mean no patron from lowliness and no patron because of lowliness. The ambiguity is controlled by grammar, not looseness: every route denies a dependency that would emerge from abasement.

topics.headline: source-cause ambiguity in the patron denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition makes lowliness the source or explanation of the denied patron relation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly marks the PP as ambiguous between noun and clause/verb attachment; CRITICAL rows preserve causal, explicative, source, and sound-binding payoffs.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive lowliness/abasement as the denied source-condition of patronage
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلذُّلِّ}} ({{tr:al-dhulli}}) is not a lowly person but the definite state of lowliness itself. The dh-l-l family can include gentleness and accessibility, as in the human humility scene of 17:24, but here {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) and {{ar:وَلِىٌّ}} ({{tr:waliyyun}}) select abasement and tractability: the bent-neck vulnerability from which a protector would be needed is excluded from God.
words.root_gloss_range: lowliness, abasement, tractability, being made submissive or easy; local phrase selects vulnerability and humiliation rather than positive gentleness

topics.headline: lowliness as impossible divine source-condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah denies the whole state of bent-neck vulnerability as a source from which God could need a patron.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after {{ar:مِّنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}); CRITICAL rows support definiteness, gerund status, vulnerability sense, 17:24 contrast, and the opposition between sovereign grip and lowliness.

words.gloss_range: coordinating pivot from negated divine relations to commanded magnification
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from what God is not to what the addressee must do. Because the ayah uses coordination rather than a narrow result particle, magnification is linked to the whole praise-and-denial complex, not just to the last clause.

topics.headline: theology turns into response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final command is joined to the denials as the response they call for.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the final imperative after the quoted praise block; CRITICAL rows treat the particle as a hinge from declarative negation to performative magnification.

words.gloss_range: Form II imperative with object suffix: declare Him great, make His greatness audible
words.prose: {{ar:كَبِّرْهُ}} ({{tr:kabbirhu}}) returns the ayah to direct command. Form II makes greatness something declared and intensified in speech, while the attached {{ar:هُ}} ({{tr:hu}}) fixes the object as God. The command does not make God greater in reality; it makes His greatness audible, echoing the rare direct magnification command of 74:3. Together with the opening say-command, it completes the ayah’s speech-performance frame.
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, largeness, growing great, declaring great; local Form II imperative selects performed declaration, not increasing God in reality

topics.headline: declare God great as final action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing imperative makes the hearer audibly declare the greatness of the very God just described as free of dependency, completing the opening say-command.
topics.reason: QAC marks Form II imperative 2ms with a direct object suffix; CRITICAL rows preserve declaration rather than ontological increase, suffix binding, closure after the triple denial, and the 74:3 echo.

words.gloss_range: Form II verbal noun as cognate accusative intensifying the magnification command
words.prose: {{ar:تَكْبِيرًۢا}} ({{tr:takbīrā}}) is the Form II verbal noun of the same root as {{ar:كَبِّرْهُ}} ({{tr:kabbirhu}}). It is not a second object; it is the cognate accusative that specifies and intensifies the act. As the final word of surah 17, it gathers the opening transcendence of 17:1, the praise frame, and the repeated k-b-r close into performed magnification.
words.root_gloss_range: greatness and declaration of greatness; local maṣdar names the performed act and intensifies its manner

topics.headline: magnification named and intensified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surah’s last word is the named act of magnification, grammatically intensifying the command that precedes it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as cognate accusative; CRITICAL rows support maṣdar force, not-second-object status, final-word closure, 17:1 frame, repeated root, tanwīn cadence, and full magnification.
